newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: G10 sees improved European growth.
newsitem.headline: G10 sees improved European growth.

text.p: Bundesbank president Hans Tietmeyer said the Group of 10 (G10) central bank governors saw improved growth in continental Europe in the first quarter of 1997.

Speaking to reporters after the monthly meeting of the G10 central bank governors, Tietmeyer also said further cyclical improvement was one important element, but further structural adjustments were necessary.
"One can see some improvement as far as growth in the first quarter, but of course the situation is different from country to country, no doubt about that," Tietmeyer said of continental Europe.

"We also feel cyclical improvement, if it continues, is one important element, but that further structural adjustment is necessary for improving the employment situation and reducing unemployment," Tietmeyer said.
He also said structural adjustments would bolster investor confidence. He said this was necessary in many continental European countries.
Tietmeyer said G10 central bank governors had discussed exchange rates at the regular monthly meeting, but he had nothing to add to what markets are doing.
"We of course discussed it (exchange rates) but I can add nothing," Tietmeyer said.
Asked about the recent decline in the dollar, Tietmeyer said he had no comment. - Zurich Editorial +41 1 631 7340
